story.originalTitle: What to expect from Honda's long-awaited F1 power unit upgrade
story.summaryEn: Honda will bring its first power unit upgrade of the 2026 Formula 1 season to Zandvoort, focusing entirely on the internal combustion engine. Chief engineer Shintaro Orihara admits engine performance is Honda's biggest weakness compared to rivals, and the new specification will also bring a fresh drivability challenge.
detailZh: 本田期待已久的F1动力单元升级有哪些看点
首席工程师折原慎太郎解释说，本田F1动力单元升级的重点完全在内燃机上。随着本田新引擎规格的引入，驾驶性将再次成为一个重要因素。
阿斯顿·马丁在匈牙利站为AMR26引入了首个重大升级包，而本田将在赞德福特站带来2026年F1赛季的首次升级。
随着阿德里安·纽维今年的首个升级包，底盘方面的差距已大幅缩小。阿斯顿·马丁距离其目标仍有很长的路要走，但Paceteq的数据显示，其在匈牙利站的正赛速度差距“仅”为每圈2.034秒。
在此前的银石和斯帕两个比赛周末，这一差距仍超过每圈5秒，不过有两点重要的说明。首先，这两条标志性赛道都长得多，而匈牙利赛道对动力单元性能的依赖也较小。
后者仍是阿斯顿·马丁的弱点，尽管本田希望凭借今年首个ADUO升级，在下半赛季开始时向前迈进一步。
该升级完全聚焦于内燃机，赛道现场总经理兼首席工程师折原慎太郎仍认为这是本田相较竞争对手的最大弱点。
“与其他制造商相比，我们的引擎性能肯定很差。所以现在最重要的改进点可能就是我们的引擎性能，因为正如我提到的，差距相当大。”
折原慎太郎，本田赛车公司赛道现场总经理兼首席工程师
“如果不提升内燃机性能，[其他方面都无济于事]。比如说，即使我们改进了能量管理，如果引擎性能很差，那也没用，”折原在接受Autosport独家采访时解释道。
“所以现在我们纯粹专注于提升引擎性能。一旦我们在那里达到目标，也许就可以优化其他一些小领域。但我们的主要关注点仍然是引擎性能，即内燃机。”
本田知道，缩小绝对动力方面的差距需要时间，这意味着在第一步之后还需要进一步的升级——一些最乐观的估计认为可提升最多30马力。
当被问及赞德福特升级的具体目标时，折原概述了一个与阿斯顿·马丁在匈牙利站类似的目标：回到所谓的“赛车场”。
这在底盘方面已经实现，但折原强调，动力单元方面也需要做到同样的事情。
“我们的目标是回到赛车场，回到这样一种状态：我们每个周末努力寻找的10毫秒或20毫秒，能够真正产生差异。”
本田新引擎面临新的驾驶性挑战
由于动力单元正在经历重大变化，赞德福特升级也带来了另一个问号。它涉及本赛季头几个月经常讨论的一个术语：驾驶性，即车手从动力单元中获得的感受。
“我们开发了工具来优化驾驶性。我们取得了良好进展，已经接近我们想要达到的目标，”折原说。
“但当我们引入规格2引擎时，燃烧特性将发生显著变化。嗯，也许不是显著，但会有很大不同。
“而且引擎在弯道阶段的行为也会改变。所以，是的，我们需要重新开发驾驶性。”
这与阿斯顿·马丁在底盘方面的升级密切相关，后者也会影响动力单元的驾驶性。
“随着赛车规格的变化，弯道速度将高得多。然后对驾驶性的要求也会改变。”
听起来本田将面临与今年年初相同的驾驶性挑战，但折原强调，这家日本制造商在任何情况下都不会回到原点。毕竟，学到的经验仍可应用于新规格。
“在上半赛季取得了很大进展。我们开发出了优化的[驾驶性]方法，”他说。
“我们将引入新引擎，可能还需要做更多工作来再次改善驾驶性，但现在我们知道该怎么做，以及应该在哪里改进。
“这是一大收获，我们可以把这一经验延续到我们的B规格引擎上。”
部分由于这一方面——驾驶性的工作——阿斯顿·马丁最近在匈牙利赛道用新动力单元进行的拍摄日如此重要。它已经为双方提供了一些初步数据可供分析，帮助他们在赞德福特避免不愉快的意外。
detailEn: What to expect from Honda's long-awaited F1 power unit upgrade

Chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explains that the focus is entirely on the internal combustion engine for Honda's F1 power unit update. Drivability will once again be an important factor with Honda's new engine specification
While Aston Martin introduced its first major upgrade package for the AMR26 in Hungary, Honda will bring its first update of the 2026 Formula 1 season to Zandvoort.

With Adrian Newey’s first upgrade package of the year, the deficit on the chassis side has been reduced considerably. Aston Martin is still a long way from where it wants to be, but figures from Paceteq show that its deficit in terms of race pace was “just” 2.034 seconds per lap in Hungary.

During the preceding weekends at Silverstone and Spa, that deficit was still more than five seconds per lap, although there are two important caveats. Firstly, both iconic circuits are much longer, while the Hungaroring is also less dependent on power unit performance.
The latter remains a weakness for Aston Martin, although Honda hopes to make a step forward at the start of the second half of the season with its first ADUO upgrade of the year.

That upgrade is entirely focused on the internal combustion engine, which general trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara still identifies as Honda's biggest weakness compared to the competition.

"Our engine performance is definitely poor compared to other manufacturers. So probably the most important point to improve now is our engine performance because, as I mentioned, the gap is quite huge.
Shintaro Orihara, Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer of Honda Racing Corporation

"Without improving our combustion engine performance, [the rest doesn’t help]. Let's say, if we improve energy management, that doesn't help if the engine performance is poor," Orihara explained during an exclusive interview with Autosport.

"So now we purely focus on improving our engine performance. Once we achieve our target there, then maybe we can optimise some other small areas. But still our main focus point is the engine performance, the combustion engine."

Honda knows that closing the deficit in terms of outright power will take time, meaning further upgrades will be required after this first step – with some of the most optimistic estimates suggesting a gain of up to 30bhp.
When asked about the specific target for the Zandvoort upgrade, Orihara outlines an objective similar to Aston Martin's in Hungary: getting back to what is referred to as the "racing field".
That has been achieved on the chassis side, but Orihara stresses that the same needs to happen on the power unit side.
"Our target is to get back to the racing field, to a situation where the 10 milliseconds or 20 milliseconds that we try so hard to find every weekend, can actually make a difference."
Honda faces fresh driveability challenge with new engine

Because the power unit is undergoing significant changes, the Zandvoort upgrade also brings another question mark. It concerns a term that has been discussed frequently during the opening months of this F1 season: drivability, the feeling the drivers get from the power unit.
"We developed our tools to optimise our driveability. We have made good progress and we were close to what we wanted to achieve," Orihara said.
"But when we introduce the spec 2 engine, the combustion characteristics will change significantly. Well, maybe not significantly, but there will be a big difference.
"And then engine behaviour will be changed in the cornering phase as well. So yeah, we need to develop our driveability again."
It goes hand in hand with Aston Martin's upgrades on the chassis side, which also have an impact on the drivability of the power unit.
"With the car spec changing, cornering speeds will be much higher. And then demands on driveability will be changing as well."

It sounds as though Honda will face the same drivability challenge it encountered at the start of this year, but Orihara stresses that the Japanese manufacturer will not be back to square one under any circumstances. After all, the lessons learned can still be applied to the new specification.
"There has been big progress through this first half of the season. We developed our optimised way [for drivability]," he said.
"We will introduce our new engine and probably we need [to do] more work to improve driveability again, but now we know how we need to do it and where we should improve.
"That has been a big learning, and we can carry over that learning point to our B spec engine."

It is partly because of this aspect – working on drivability – that Aston Martin's recent filming day at the Hungaroring with the new power unit was so important. It has already provided both parties with some initial data to analyse, helping them avoid unpleasant surprises at Zandvoort.

relatedItems.originalTitle: Christian Horner proposes major change to how fans watch F1
relatedItems.summaryEn: Former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Formula 1 should let fans sit virtually on their favourite team's pitwall and hear how strategy calls are made.
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳建议对F1车迷的观赛方式做出重大改变
克里斯蒂安·霍纳建议让F1车迷以虚拟方式进入车队指挥台（pitwall），从而更深入地了解比赛策略与决策过程
赛道之外的赛车文化。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计，以及那些让赛车超越运动本身的故事。
前红牛车队首席执行官兼领队克里斯蒂安·霍纳主张，F1应允许车迷以虚拟方式坐进自己支持车队的指挥台（pitwall），听到策略决定是如何做出的。
霍纳在2025年7月离开红牛后，在过去15个月里以车迷身份观看大奖赛，这是他职业生涯中的第一次。
周三在纽约举行的汽车运动商业交流会上发言时，这位英国人表示，维修区指挥台所知与电视观众所见之间的差距令他感到惊讶。
汽车运动商业交流会在纽约市迎来第二届，汇聚了来自赛车运动、商业和品牌领域的高层领袖，地点设在曼哈顿汽车展厅，共同探讨赛车运动在美国的发展。
克里斯蒂安·霍纳自离开甲骨文红牛车队以来首次在美国出席该活动。
其他小组成员还包括七届纳斯卡杯系列赛冠军吉米·约翰逊、前一级方程式董事长兼首席执行官蔡斯·凯里、通用汽车的马克·罗伊斯、潘世奇的乔纳森·吉布森以及纳斯卡的蒂姆·克拉克。
“但对我来说，这也是一种不同的视角。作为一名车迷、一名观众，突然听着我25年都没听过的解说员解说比赛，突然感觉……从维修区墙上那个充满各种信息、知识、策略和对手分析等的茧房里，突然之间你只有屏幕，解说员在解释发生了什么，还有不同的图形，”他说。
“感觉他们本可以揭开更多内幕。车队对此抵制，因为他们不想泄露知识产权和竞争优势。但看看现在观众消费的方式，以及他们对数据和信息的渴望与热切，从我坐在维修区墙上的经历突然变成一名观众，对手分析和策略以及比赛走势的呈现、还有沟通交流，可获取的内容之多令人惊叹。
红牛车队成员在维修区墙上
"显然，这些都在指挥台（pitwall）上进行等等。所以我真的觉得这是一个可以进一步开发的领域，让观众获得更好的体验。"
当被问及如何为车迷实现这一点时，霍纳补充道："也许可以做成互动式的。为什么不虚拟地坐在你最喜欢的车队的指挥台上，了解他们是如何做出决定的、他们正在进行哪些讨论。
"现在，作为一支车队，我会反对这样做，因为你不想把那些信息泄露出去。但归根结底，体育就是娱乐，现在竞争如此激烈，一级方程式已经把自己带到了这个不可思议的位置，当然是通过Netflix系列剧，我们拥有了这一整代新的车迷和不同类型的车迷。
"它必须不断进化。它不能停滞不前，而且它现在处于如此好的位置。它不能原地踏步，我相信它不会，但你必须不断进化。"
detailEn: Christian Horner proposes major change to how fans watch F1
Christian Horner has suggested giving F1 fans virtual access to team pitwalls to offer greater insight into race strategies and decision-making
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner argued that Formula 1 should let fans sit on their favourite team's pitwall virtually and hear how strategy calls are made.
Horner has spent the past 15 months watching grands prix as a fan for the first time in his career, after leaving Red Bull in July 2025.
Speaking at the Autosport Business Exchange in New York on Wednesday, the Briton said the gap between what the pitwall knows and what TV viewers see had surprised him.

Autosport Business Exchange returned to New York City for its second edition, bringing together senior leaders from across motorsport, business and brands at the Manhattan Motorcars showroom to examine racing's growth in America
Christian Horner made his first U.S. appearance at the event since leaving Oracle Red Bull Racing

Other panellists included seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, former chairman and CEO of Formula 1 Chase Carey, General Motors' Mark Reuss, Penske's Jonathan Gibson and NASCAR's Tim Clark

"But for me, it was also a different perspective. As a fan, as a spectator, suddenly watching races with commentators that I hadn't heard for 25 years and suddenly feeling... Going from that sort of cocoon on the pitwall with all that information and knowledge and strategies and competitor analysis and so on, suddenly you've just got the screen with the commentators explaining what's going on and different graphics," he said.

"It felt like there's so much more that they could lift the lid on. The teams fight against it because they don't want to give the IP away and a competitive advantage. But just looking at how viewers consume now and their hunger and eagerness for data and information, going from the experience that I had from sitting on the pitwall to suddenly being a viewer, it's amazing just how much more is available in terms of competitor analysis and strategy and how races are shaping up, and the communication.
Red Bull Racing team members on the pit wall
"Obviously, that's going on on the pitwall and so on. So I really feel that that's an area that could be further exploited to get the viewer an even better experience."

When asked how that could be done for fans, Horner added: "Maybe make it interactive. Why not sit on the pitwall, virtually, of your favourite team, understand how they're getting to the decisions that they are, the discussions that they're having.

"Now, as a team, I would have argued against that because you don't want to be giving that information away. But, at the end of the day, sport is entertainment and there's so much competition now that Formula 1 has got itself into this incredible place where, certainly through the Netflix series, we've got this whole new generation and variants of fans.
"It's got to keep evolving. It can't stagnate and it's in such a great spot. It can't stand still, which I'm sure it's not going to, but you've got to keep evolving."
keyPointsZh: 霍纳是在纽约举行的Autosport Business Exchange活动上发言时提出这一建议的

keyPointsEn: Horner made the suggestion while speaking at the Autosport Business Exchange in New York
He raised the idea as a way to give fans greater insight into race strategies and decision-making
